title: Plant growth and resources
objective: Make plants live off their environment: they grow where climate allows, compete for limited resources, age and die.
acceptance_criteria: Plants gain energy from the resources of their cell; the gain depends on the cell's current temperature and water.
Test: the same plant grows more slowly, or not at all, in a cell that is too cold or too dry than in a favourable cell.
Resources per cell are limited, so plants in the same place compete and growth cannot be unlimited.
Plants age and die of old age, lack of energy or hostile climate.
The documentation states where plant energy comes from and what limits it; no energy appears without such a source.
Genome-derived traits influence growth or tolerance.
decisions: The resource model (light, water, nutrients or a simplification).
ecology_ideas: Cell resources (water, nutrients or a single 'fertility' value) that are used up by growth and regenerate slowly up to a cap set by the climate: this gives logistic growth, so plants stop at a carrying capacity instead of exploding or vanishing.
Growth that slows as a cell gets crowded, so dense patches level off.
Plants keeping a reserve (roots) that survives grazing, so a grazed plant can regrow.
